title: Optimization and Simulation of Flat Area Sites Based on Probability Matching and Transfer Intensity Using Remote Sensing Precipitation
content:
Abstract

The accuracy and continuity of records from rain gauge networks, as critical sources of precipitation data, directly influence the reliability of subsequent meteorological, land surface, and hydrological studies. Despite generally high recording accuracy, the sparse distribution of sites within these networks is prevalent. Achieving a balance between precision and enhanced spatial coverage of precipitation records remains a substantial challenge. This study proposes a method to densifying and estimating point precipitation by integrating remote sensing data with probability matching and transfer intensity techniques, thus augmenting the information content of rain gauge networks. Focusing on three flat zones in eastern China, the study analyzed the probability distribution characteristics of precipitation from remote sensing data and observation sites. It further explored the synergistic effects of weighted cosine similarity and information entropy transfer quantification in precipitation estimation. The results showed a high consistency in probability distribution between remote sensing precipitation at observation and estimation sites. Additionally, information entropy increased progressively from observation sites to estimation sites and then to remote sensing precipitation. Evaluation indices revealed that the estimated sites achieved the TSS (Taylor skill score) ranging from 0.81 to 0.84, the NSE (Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency) from 0.79 to 0.91. The average KGE (Kling-Gupta efficiency), POD (probability of detection), and FAR (false alarm ratio) were 0.82, 0.93, and 0.21, respectively, indicating high accuracy. This study effectively combines remote sensing data with probability-uncertainty theory to provide more extensive precipitation information across regional scales, offering robust support for investigating precipitation patterns and their variability.
